title: Back by Lunch

pre.en: Why does Chen have to go to the dentist?
pre.zh: 小陈为什么得去看牙医？
options: He fell over in the office.
He has a check-up every year.
He broke a tooth on something Tom made.

intro: 小陈晚上给组长 Rachel 打电话：吃 Tom 做的太妃糖把牙咬裂了，明天上午得去看牙医。他在电话里把手上的事一件件交代清楚。读的时候留意 make、let、help 后面怎么接：making me come、let you decide、help you find，动词前面都不加 to。

sentences.en: Hi, Rachel. Sorry to ring so late.
sentences.zh: 喂，Rachel，这么晚打给你，不好意思。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: I'm afraid I'll be out of the office tomorrow morning.
sentences.zh: 明天上午我恐怕来不了办公室了。

sentences.en: Oh no. What's happened?
sentences.zh: 啊，怎么了？
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: I cracked a tooth on Tom's homemade toffee at dinner.
sentences.zh: 晚饭吃 Tom 自己做的太妃糖，把一颗牙咬裂了。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: And my dentist's making me come in at ten.
sentences.zh: 牙医让我明天十点过去。

sentences.en: I'll probably be back by about one.
sentences.zh: 大概一点左右能回来。

sentences.en: Ouch. Poor you.
sentences.zh: 哎哟，真够倒霉的。
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: I don't want anyone to get the wrong idea, so here's the plan.
sentences.zh: 我不想让大家误会，所以先把安排说清楚。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: I've handed the login screen over to Mia.
sentences.zh: 登录页我已经交给 Mia 了。

sentences.en: And I've asked her to let Arjun know when the tests pass.
sentences.zh: 也让她等测试过了跟 Arjun 说一声。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 好。
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: Arjun's kindly offered to cover for me at the eleven o'clock call with the client.
sentences.zh: Arjun 人很好，主动说十一点跟客户的电话会帮我顶一下。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: And I'll let you decide whether to move Friday's demo.
sentences.zh: 周五的演示要不要改期，你来定。

sentences.en: Just don't forget to tell the client.
sentences.zh: 就是别忘了通知客户。

sentences.en: Will do.
sentences.zh: 知道了。
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: And if anything comes up?
sentences.zh: 那要是有什么事呢？

sentences.en: Then please get in touch with me by text, not by phone.
sentences.zh: 那就发短信联系我，别打电话。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: The dentist will make me keep my mouth open.
sentences.zh: 牙医会让我一直张着嘴。

sentences.en: So I'll be on mute anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正我也是「静音」状态。

sentences.en: I'll reply on the way back.
sentences.zh: 我回来的路上再回你。

sentences.en: Ha. OK.
sentences.zh: 哈，好。
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: I'll also send you a list of my six open tasks to help you find everything.
sentences.zh: 我还会发你一张清单，列出我手上六件没做完的事，方便你找。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: The most urgent one is the crash on the settings page.
sentences.zh: 最急的是设置页的闪退。

sentences.en: And I'll finish writing the release notes tonight.
sentences.zh: 发版说明我今晚写完。

sentences.en: Sorry, you must be fed up with my lists by now.
sentences.zh: 不好意思，我的清单你大概早就听烦了。

sentences.en: I hope this all makes sense.
sentences.zh: 希望我说清楚了。

sentences.en: Chen, it's a filling, not a holiday.
sentences.zh: 小陈，你这是去补个牙，又不是去度假。
sentences.speaker: Rachel

sentences.en: But to be honest, this is the best handover we've ever had.
sentences.zh: 不过说实话，这是我们有过的最好的一次交接。

sentences.en: And please tell Tom his toffee is now banned from the office.
sentences.zh: 还有，麻烦转告 Tom，他的太妃糖从此不许带进办公室。

sentences.en: Could you do one of these for my two weeks in Spain?
sentences.zh: 我去西班牙那两个星期，你也帮我弄一份这样的交接吧？

cards.zh: 恐怕；（客气地说出坏消息）
cards.note: used to politely say something that the other person may not want to hear
cards.tip: 开头先说 I'm afraid，后面的坏消息就软了一点；不是「我害怕」。
cards.example: I'm afraid the meeting room is booked all afternoon.

cards.zh: 不在办公室；外出（不上班）
cards.note: to be away from work, for example on holiday or at an appointment
cards.tip: 自动回复邮件里最常见：out-of-office reply。只说人不在，不说明原因，比 I'm absent 自然得多。
cards.example: I'm out of the office until Monday, so please email Sam.

cards.note: crack a tooth 把牙咬裂；名词也是 crack（裂缝）：a crack in the screen。
homemade bread / cake；反义是 shop-bought（店里买的）。
用黄油和糖熬的硬糖，英国很常见，咬起来很黏、很硬。
to give work or responsibility for something to another person
cards.tip: 交给谁用 to；代词放中间：hand it over to Mia。名词 handover 就是「交接」。
cards.example: Before her holiday, she handed the project over to me.

cards.zh: 告诉某人一声；通知某人
cards.tip: 比 tell 更随和，邮件结尾常用：Let me know what you think. know 前面不加 to。
cards.example: Let me know if you need anything else.

cards.note: 放在动词前，表示对方帮忙是出于好意：kindly offered 好心主动提出。也常用来客气地请求：Could you kindly …?
to do someone's work while they are away
cards.tip: for 后面接被顶替的人；也有「替某人打掩护」的意思，要看上下文。
cards.example: Can you cover for me on Friday? I've got a doctor's appointment.

cards.zh: 有什么事的话；万一出了状况
cards.note: if something happens that needs attention, especially something you did not plan for
cards.tip: come up 是「（意外地）出现」；if 从句里用一般现在时 comes，不用 will come。
cards.example: I'll be at home all day, so call me if anything comes up.

cards.note: to contact someone by phone, email or message
cards.tip: 说的是「联系上」这个动作；保持联系是 keep in touch（第 4 课）。
cards.example: Please get in touch with our support team if the app stops working.

cards.note: if you are on mute in a call, other people cannot hear you
cards.tip: 本来说开会时关了麦；这里拿来开玩笑：张着嘴看牙，想说话也说不了。
cards.example: Sorry, I was on mute — can you hear me now?

cards.tip: on the way back 回来的路上；on the way home 回家路上，home 前不加 to。
cards.example: Can you pick up some milk on the way home?

cards.note: to be annoyed or bored with something that has gone on for too long
to have a clear meaning that is easy to understand
have a filling 补牙。也指食物的馅：pie filling。
used before you say what you really think, especially something the listener may not like
来自 hand over；write a handover 写交接文档。
